tools.name: trackly_search_jobs
tools.description: Search and filter job postings. Returns one matching page with title, company, location, structured fields and backend pagination. Use jobFunctions for multiple roles, region for multiple regions, and usStates/caProvinces for geographic detail. Work arrangement is independent from geography and employment type. Unknown sponsorship and non-comparable salary data stay visible with exclude_no and salaryFloorUsd. Never invent industry, specialization, exclusion or literal-search controls; ask when sponsorship intent is ambiguous. A numeric total with totalIsLowerBound=true (also in pagination) is only a lower bound. If the total is unavailable, returned matching jobs remain valid. Explain countGuidance and use hasMore/pagination; do not retry just for totals. matchScoreStatus=pending identifies owned waiting work for the current parsed resume and selected description: retryable description parsing or a live job-specific score item. Otherwise a missing score remains not_scored. Explain matchScoreReason: parse_required and score_required describe prerequisites, outside_scoring_window means outside the automatic 30-day window, description_unavailable means no usable description, inactive means a closed posting, and not_scored means unknown. Never estimate a missing numeric score.

function.description: Job function filter. One of: product, engineering, design, data, marketing, sales, partnerships, finance, strategy, operations, people, legal, support, other

jobFunctions.description: Multiple job functions, combined with OR. Use instead of function. Omit both to request all 14 functions.

companyId.description: Filter jobs by company ID (get from trackly_search_companies)

region.description: Region tags combined with OR, including us. Use instead of locationFilter; this avoids its legacy mixed-US list limitation. Geographic child behavior follows the backend location rollout.

usStates.description: US state codes, DC, PR, or REMOTE. Multiple values select alternatives. REMOTE alongside codes also includes remote jobs. Under canonical location enforcement children select their parent; legacy rollout keeps compatibility behavior. Do not combine with remote=true.

caProvinces.description: Canadian province/territory codes or REMOTE. Multiple values select alternatives. REMOTE alongside codes also includes remote jobs. Parent-scoped OR requires canonical location enforcement. Do not combine with remote=true.

internshipLevels.description: Internship education levels, combined with OR: undergraduate, graduate, mba, not_specified. Applies to internships in jobModality=internship or all; full-time jobs remain unaffected. This does not change the saved/default modality: set jobModality explicitly when you want internships.

favoriteCompaniesOnly.description: true limits results to your favorited companies; false explicitly disables this restriction.

postedWithinDays.description: Posting-recency window in days: 1, 3, 7, 14, or 30; 0 disables the saved window. Uses the backend discovery-date policy; not an incremental-sync cursor. Omitted uses the saved/default window only when status is omitted, new, or all; explicit pipeline statuses skip that saved window. Explicit values apply in every view.

salaryFloorUsd.description: Annual USD minimum salary floor. Excludes comparable listed annual-USD minimums below this amount; unknown, hourly and non-USD salaries remain visible. 0 disables the floor. Omitted uses saved/default preferences only when status is omitted, new, or all; explicit pipeline statuses skip the saved floor. Explicit values apply in every view. This is not a guaranteed salary threshold.

since.description: Incremental sync: jobs first seen by Trackly since this ISO-8601 date/timestamp, not employer posting dates. Must be within the past 90 days and not in the future; backend validates the range. Prefer a timestamp with timezone. Since does not reset filters. Saved posting and salary constraints apply only when status is omitted, new, or all; use postedWithinDays=0 and salaryFloorUsd=0 to disable them. Explicit pipeline views skip saved filters; explicit request filters still apply.

locationFilter.description: Region tag filter. Pass ONE of: (a) a single scalar from 'us', 'non_us', 'all', or a REGION_TAGS value ('europe', 'latam', 'middle_east', 'asia', 'africa', 'canada', 'oceania', 'remote', 'unknown'); or (b) an array of region tags for multi-region (e.g. ['europe', 'canada']). The array form excludes 'us' — combining 'us' with other tags causes the backend to silently drop the others. For 'not US' use the scalar 'non_us' alone.

jobModality.description: Employment type (NOT work arrangement). full_time = full-time roles, internship = internships, all = both. Use workArrangements for remote, hybrid, or in-person classification.

workArrangements.description: Work arrangement filter, independent from geography and employment type. Values: remote, hybrid, in_person, unspecified. Multiple values use OR semantics.

roleTypes.description: Role type filter: corporate (default), frontline (store, warehouse, food service, driving, security, skilled trades, care aides), or both. Omitted uses the student's saved preference. Applies to status new and all; pipeline views (applied_confirmed, check_later, not_interested) are never filtered by role type.

remote.description: Filter to global remote-only jobs (maps to usStates=REMOTE). Do not combine with region/locationFilter or geographic child arrays. For remote work within a region, use workArrangements=["remote"] with region instead.

status.description: Filter by YOUR application pipeline state. Not a generic job-posting status. Values: new, applied_confirmed, check_later, not_interested, all

sort.description: Sort order: newest (default) or match (highest match score first; requires resume). Backend rejects legacy oldest/company with HTTP 400.

sponsorship.description: Visa sponsorship: all applies no filter; exclude_no removes reliable explicit no statements and keeps yes plus unknown/not mentioned; only_yes requires reliable explicit yes and excludes unknown. 'Not no' means exclude_no, never only_yes. Ask when intent is ambiguous. Filtering requires status=new (defaulted when omitted); the backend ignores sponsorship on other pipeline views.

limit.description: Page size, integer 1-100; MCP default 20 for concise agent results. Request up to the full API limit of 100 when needed.

offset.description: Pagination offset, non-negative integer. Keep filters and sort unchanged when paging; live catalog changes can move rows.

keywords.description: Legacy keyword search. Title/company/location matches are supported; description recall depends on the backend provider. Not a guaranteed full-catalog literal/phrase/exclusion search.

tools.name: trackly_create_tracker_application
tools.description: Add a job to the Tracker board (Quick Add) when it has no Tracker entry yet. Creating an entry records the job as applied: the new entry starts in the applied stage, dated appliedOn when given. Only call it after the user explicitly confirms they applied, and pass explicitUserConfirmed=true. Pass jobId, or companyName and roleTitle. Move the entry afterwards with trackly_update_tracker_stage, for example to interview. If the job, or the same company and role, is already on the board, nothing is written and the existing entry is returned with created=false. A repeated call never adds a second entry. Separate from trackly_update_status, which only sets the job list status.

jobId.description: Trackly job posting ID. The company, role, location and default link come from the Trackly job. Pass jobId, or companyName and roleTitle (or both, to override the job's names).

companyName.description: Company name, up to 200 characters. Required with roleTitle when there is no jobId; with a jobId it overrides the job's company name.

roleTitle.description: Role title, up to 200 characters. Required with companyName when there is no jobId; with a jobId it overrides the job's title.

appliedOn.description: Date the user applied, YYYY-MM-DD, read as a local date in America/Los_Angeles. Omit when unknown.

link.description: Posting or application URL, http(s), up to 2048 characters. Defaults to the Trackly job's URL when jobId is given.

explicitUserConfirmed.description: Must be true: the user explicitly confirmed they applied to this job, because creating a Tracker entry records the job as applied.

tools.name: trackly_update_tracker_stage
tools.description: Move one Tracker entry to a new stage (for example rejected or interview), as if the user dragged the card on the /tracker board, with the same history, undo and conflict checks. Pass exactly one of applicationId or jobId. This is separate from trackly_update_status, which only sets the job list status: marking an entry rejected here keeps its Applied record and does not discard the job. There is no "paused" stage: record a pause with trackly_add_tracker_note and leave the stage unchanged. If the entry is already in that stage nothing is written. Returns not_found when the job has no Tracker entry yet (this tool never creates one; use trackly_create_tracker_application first), tracker_unavailable when the Tracker is switched off, and version_conflict with the entry's current version and stage if it kept changing; nothing is written on any error.

jobId.description: Trackly job posting ID. Resolved to its Tracker entry. Pass exactly one of applicationId or jobId.

note.description: Optional dated note saved after the stage change, up to 1000 characters. Say where the evidence came from, for example "rejection email, Nov 9".

tools.name: trackly_retract_tracker_event
tools.description: Undo one Tracker event that the user names: retract a single stage change, note or other event by its eventId, as the undo on the /tracker board does. Only call it when the user asked to undo that specific event; never to clean up or to retry. The event stays in history marked as retracted and the entry's stage is recomputed. Retracting an already retracted event changes nothing. The only stage event of an entry, and a retraction itself, cannot be retracted. Returns not_found, tracker_unavailable or version_conflict without writing anything.
